squared-euclidean-distance.name: Squared Euclidean distance
squared-euclidean-distance.definition: The sum of squared coordinate differences between two vectors.
squared-euclidean-distance.explanation: Squared distance ranks neighbors in the same order as Euclidean distance because square root is increasing. It avoids an unnecessary square root during search. Distance depends on feature units and representation, so scaling and category encoding define what the algorithm treats as similar. Nonfinite coordinates must be rejected before sorting. Equal feature weights remain a modeling choice. Document the chosen geometry.

standardization.name: Standardization
standardization.definition: Centering a feature by its training mean and scaling by its training standard deviation.
standardization.explanation: Standardization puts numeric features on comparable scales, which is crucial for distance-based models. Scaler::fit estimates mean and deviation only from training rows; Scaler::transform applies those stored values without refitting. A constant feature has zero deviation, so the project uses scale one and maps its training values to zero. A differing query then adds the same distance contribution to every training point and cannot distinguish neighbors. Validation, test, and inference features never update the fitted scaler.

knn.name: k-nearest neighbors
knn.definition: A classifier that votes among the k closest labeled training points.
knn.explanation: Knn::fit validates and stores labeled training vectors, k, and the class count; it does not perform optimizer steps or estimate weights. Knn::predict calculates squared distances, selects the k closest rows, and returns a discrete label. Distances are raw ranking quantities, not probabilities or task predictions. Small k follows local detail and noise; larger k smooths boundaries. Validation should choose k. Direct inference grows with the number of stored rows, and tie handling must be deterministic.

naive-bayes.name: Naive Bayes
naive-bayes.definition: A probabilistic classifier assuming features are conditionally independent given the class.
naive-bayes.explanation: The assumption factorizes a joint class likelihood into a product of per-feature likelihoods. This makes fitting and prediction cheap even when the independence claim is approximate. Correlated features can count the same evidence more than once and produce overconfident scores, so held-out accuracy and calibration should be checked. Class priors also change when training prevalence changes. Use logarithms for stable products.

gaussian-naive-bayes.name: Gaussian naive Bayes
gaussian-naive-bayes.definition: Naive Bayes using a Gaussian likelihood for each numeric feature within each class.
gaussian-naive-bayes.explanation: GaussianNb::fit estimates a prior, mean, and population variance for every class-feature pair. GaussianNb::predict adds log Gaussian densities and the log prior, then returns the discrete label with the greatest raw log score. The project does not normalize those scores into probabilities. A variance floor prevents division by zero for constant features. This compact model may poorly describe skewed, multimodal, or correlated data. A probability-returning extension would need stable normalization and held-out calibration checks.
